title: SM in the Wild: Measuring Security-Semantics Failures in Chinese Commercial Cryptography Implementations
description: Chinese commercial cryptography (Guomi: SM2, SM3, SM4) exposes security inputs that international APIs and misuse taxonomies omit: the signer's identity, the curve and the ciphertext arrangement. We call this gap contract impedance mismatch and measure it in published software, not deployments. We build an executable SM2/SM3/SM4 oracle calibrated against four GB/T standards and two Bouncy Castle defects. Over three corpora (npm, Maven, Gitee) we find 147 adjudicated rows, which reduce to 64 finding keys (§5). Confirmation is single-author and LLM-assisted, not independent human validation, and the 144 confirmed pairs come from a re-coding of all 270 candidates after a first pass that confirmed 17 (§6.1). Every demonstrated confidentiality break is a generic defect (known key, fixed IV, non-cryptographic randomness), including a JCA SM4 provider that replaces caller IVs with a constant; the Guomi-specific categories yield conformance defects and permitted-but-weak defaults. Four detector families find 9 of a curated 28-finding cohort, all hard-coded keys; none flags any Guomi-specific property. On 88 seeded defects our literal screen localises 37.5% and Semgrep's semantic screen 10.2%; neither localises the 12 provider-contract defects. Constant screens find implementations, not uses, and a frame's membership rate must precede its precision. Prepared for submission to USENIX Security 2027 (Cycle 2). Artefacts whose findings are not already public are pseudonymized (U1-U61) per the paper's Ethical Considerations section.
